title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 105-109): Grothendieck is axiomatising a 'tame' or stratified topology without points. Its objects are 'multistructures' (closed stratified pieces X with 'interiors' X°). He uses order relations ≤ and ≪ (the latter tied to 'ombres' Omb(X)). On the previous page he compares two candidate structures on a set M.

(i) ≰-mégations: the primitive data are order and non-inclusion relations, the 'ensembliste' or Σ-point of view, governed by axioms AtL1, AtL2, AtL3 and AtC(spec).

(ii) |∘|-mégations: the primitive datum is a binary relation X|∘|Y, read 'X and Y stratifiedly disjoint', i.e. X°∩Y°=∅, subject to condition (****).

Page 107 establishes two things. First, on the common domain the two notions are equivalent: ≰-mégations satisfying AtL1-3 and AtC(spec) correspond to |∘|-mégations satisfying (****). Second, AtL1 makes both too restrictive.

Page 108 draws the conclusion. There are two possible generalisations 'in the direction of a topology without divisibility axiom'. The |∘| direction is the richer one, for two reasons:
- it always induces a corresponding ≰-structure;
- it carries in addition an intrinsic disjointness notion that expresses a palpable geometric intuition. Without AtL1, this notion cannot be recovered from the ≰-point of view alone.

In retrospect, the axiom AtC(spec) looks artificial. It reflects the predicament of someone who can express 'disjointness' only through the set-like structures X°. Hence a change of viewpoint: the strings of axioms AtC(spec), AtC, AtD... 'fall with a flat thud', and he restarts from scratch. On the next page he defines a 'magazin' as a set M with three primitive relations ≤, ≪ and |∘|.

The page proves nothing. It is a methodological decision: take disjointness as a primitive relation rather than derive it from point-set data. This is a design choice in a point-free, region-based axiomatics of stratified spaces.
errors: No mathematical claim is proved on this page. The assertion that the |∘| approach 'always' yields a ≰-structure is stated without verification. It depends on axioms (Mag 4-5 etc.) that are being rewritten on the following page.

ideas.what: Taking a primitive binary 'disjointness of interiors' relation |∘| on pieces of a space, rather than deriving it from set-theoretic interiors, as the basis for a point-free axiomatics of tame/stratified topology.
ideas.modern_name: Region-based (mereotopological) topology; contact/connection algebras (the complement of a contact relation is a disjointness relation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), de Vries (1962) proximity/compingent algebras; Clarke (1981); Randell–Cui–Cohn RCC (1992); Düntsch–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the 'magazin' / mégation axiomatics is unpublished as far as known

ideas.what: Comparison and partial equivalence (on a common domain) between an order/non-inclusion-based structure (≰-mégations with AtL1-3, AtC(spec)) and a disjointness-based structure (|∘|-mégations with (****)), with the judgment that the latter is strictly richer once AtL1 is dropped.
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of axiomatisations of point-free spaces (frames/locales vs. contact algebras)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Locale theory (Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone); de Vries duality

ideas.what: Dropping the 'divisibility' axiom: a topology-like structure in which pieces need not be subdivisible.
ideas.modern_name: Non-atomless / finite stratified structures; cf. o-minimal cell decompositions as finite combinatorial data

missed.claim: Grothendieck's decision to make 'stratified disjointness' a primitive relation in his tame-topology axiomatics parallels the mereotopological and contact-algebra tradition (Whitehead, de Laguna, de Vries, RCC, Düntsch–Vakarelov). That tradition was developed independently and is never linked to his 'topologie modérée' programme. The literature on tame topology (o-minimality) and the literature on point-free region-based topology have not been connected through these notes.
missed.quote: une notion |∘| de disjonction intrinsèque, qui exprime une intuition géométrique palpable, laquelle échappe (vu l'absence de AtL1) au seul ≰-point de vue
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A contact-algebra style axiomatisation of stratified or o-minimal spaces (regions = definable closed sets, with disjointness of strata interiors as primitive) could give a point-free foundation of tame topology closer to Grothendieck's intent than o-minimal structures.

missed.claim: The 'magazin' axiomatics (M, ≤, ≪, |∘|) that replaces the abandoned AtC/AtD systems was never completed or published. Its relation to the Esquisse's tame-topology wish (stratified spaces, dévissage) remains unexplored.
missed.quote: les ribambelles d'axiomes de toutes sortes AtC(spec), AtC, AtD ... tombent ... je reprends tout, encore une fois!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete unpublished attempt at Grothendieck's point-free tame topology; it could be compared with o-minimal and stratified-space categories.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a methodological pivot rather than a result. Still, it documents unpublished detail of Grothendieck's 1986 point-free tame-topology axiomatics: choosing disjointness as primitive and discarding earlier axiom systems. The parallel with mereotopology and contact algebras is not discussed in the literature as far as I know, but the content is fragmentary.
transcription_corrections: 'une dérivation d'une topologie' is more likely 'en direction d'une topologie sans axiome de divisibilité'; similarly 'c'est la direction |∘| qui me semble la plus riche' (not 'dérivation |·|').
'Σ-ensembles' / 'Σ-point de vue': the symbol is the struck relation used on p.107 (≰), so read 'structure de ≰-mégation correspondante' and 'au seul ≰-point de vue'.
'qui ne dispose d'une notion de "disjonction" en termes des "structures ensemblistes" X°' likely reads '...que en termes des "structures ensemblistes" X°'.

Last lines likely: 'Donc finalement, je change d'optique — les ribambelles d'axiomes de toutes sortes AtC(spec), AtC, AtD ... tombent avec un bruit flasque, je reprends [tout, encore une fois!]', continuing on p.109 ('but, un con une fois!' probably 'tout, encore une fois!').
The relation symbol is |∘| (as on pp.107, 109), not |·|.
'AL1' should read 'AtL1'; 'AC, AD' should read 'AtC, AtD'.
